newsitem.title: UK: Med gasoline up $13, other products mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: Med gasoline up $13, other products mostly steady.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products saw little change in values on Monday with the exception of gasoline, which gained in line with a $13 jump in cargo values in the north.
The Med gasoline market was quieter than in NWE but just as tight and saw notional gains at least on a par with the gains seen on NWE cargoes on the day.
One Med trader referred to a shortage of Greek and Isreali export volumes, Italian purchasing of Eurograde and exports of lower-quality gasolines.
A French refiner was heard seeking volumes for Lebanon and having to search for in the north, rather than the Med.
The naphtha market was quiet, with levels steady in the $186-$189 CIF Med range for cargoes.
Gas oil was looking a touch firmer with talk that recent plentiful Russian supplies were drying up with fears Italy is nearly sold-out until mid to late August.
Traders said Italian heating oil was pegged around fob high quotes +3-3.50 with unconfirmed talk of an Italian selling at high fob quotes +$3.
High sulphur cracked cargoes were a little weaker, offered at $91 and $90 cif for poorer quality material with little buying interest seen. One trader said he bid $88.
"The market is weaker. There's some demand into the barge market but cracked cargoes are under pressure," one trader said.

But scarce bunker spec remains steady with traders saying it will continue to fetch $100. High sulphur straight-run was said to have traded at a $3 premium to high cif Med quotes on Monday, with a cargo bought by an Italian refiner out of Mersin.
One percent remains quiet with traders saying a large buyer will be eyeing fewer cargoes for August.
"If somebody has a low sulphur cargo, he will sell into barges and get better value," one trader said.
